title: Monitoring the three: which metric means trouble in each

videos.script: A database in trouble often looks calm from outside. The processor is idle. The memory graph is flat. And a secondary is eighteen seconds behind, or a read is wading through two thousand deleted rows to return ten. {{calm}} Each of the three servers in this course reports on itself. MongoDB answers serverStatus. Redis answers INFO. Cassandra answers nodetool. Between them, that is several hundred numbers. {{hundreds}} This lesson picks the few that decide something, and makes each one move. You will fill a small cache and watch it fill. {{cache}} You will freeze a replica and measure how far behind it falls, in seconds and in bytes. {{replica}} You will find a slow query while it runs, and kill it. {{slow}} Then the harder question. Which of these numbers should wake somebody at three in the morning? Very few. The ones that mean data is about to be lost, or work is being refused. {{page}} The rest go on a dashboard, for the person who was woken to read.
